transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you too, Dr. Smith. Well, I'm here because... for almost two years now, I've been dealing with a situation at work that I just can't shake. I'm a music director, and right after this one commission, I became certain that a few people in the ensemble started quietly trying to undermine my work. 

It's not always obvious, but it's in the details. They use sudden schedule changes, specific seating choices, and just... little comments they make during rehearsals. They'll show me emails or notes that supposedly explain why things had to be changed, but I know what's really going on. It's been going on for a long time, and I guess I just needed to talk to someone about it.
Aside from the belief that your colleagues are undermining you, have you ever heard voices or seen things that others could not perceive?

No, I haven't experienced anything like that. I don't hear voices or see things that aren't there. It's really just... the actual, tangible things they're doing at work. But no, my hearing and vision are completely normal.
Do you find that you feel this same way about people in other areas of your life, such as with friends or family members, or is this feeling strictly limited to these specific colleagues at work?

No, it's really just limited to those specific colleagues. I don't feel that way about my friends or my family at all. 

Honestly, outside of this whole issue with the ensemble, everything else is fine. I still meet my deadlines, I keep up with my composing... I even go for a run most mornings. And things at home with my wife are basically steady. So it really is just confined to that one situation at work.

Have you ever tried to confront these colleagues directly about these actions, or have you discussed these suspicions with anyone else, such as your wife or a supervisor, to see if they perceive the situation the same way you do?

No, I haven't confronted them. I... I guess I just don't want to cause a big scene during rehearsals or make the working environment even more difficult than it already is. 

And as for talking to anyone else, like my wife or a supervisor... no, I haven't really brought it up to them either. I've mostly just kept it to myself. I think that's why I finally decided to come in and talk to you about it, just to get it out in the open with someone.
Are there any other beliefs or ideas you hold that others might find difficult to believe or seem unusual, even if they aren't related to your colleagues?

No, not at all. I mean... I don't have any other unusual ideas or beliefs. Everything else in my life is just, you know, completely normal. It really is just that specific situation with the ensemble. I don't hold any strange views about anything else.

If your wife or a neutral third party were to look at the emails and notes you mentioned, do you think they would agree that these actions are intended to undermine you, or do you think they might interpret them differently?

I suppose... if my wife or someone else looked at them, they might actually interpret them differently. They might just see what's written on the surface and believe the excuses. 

And I guess that's really why I’m here. Because for almost two years now, ever since that commission, I’ve been completely unable to shake the certainty that a few people in the ensemble are quietly undermining my work. They use these sudden schedule changes, seating choices, and little comments in rehearsals to do it. Even when they show me emails or notes that supposedly explain it all away... I just know what they're actually doing. So, a neutral person might buy their explanations, but I know what's really going on.
Aside from your work, have you noticed any changes in your ability to socialize, maintain your hygiene, or manage your daily responsibilities since this situation began two years ago?

No, not really. Outside of this whole issue with the ensemble... everything else is fine. I still meet my deadlines and keep up with my composing. I even still go for a run most mornings. And things at home with my wife are basically steady. So, no, I haven't noticed any changes in how I take care of myself or handle my normal, day-to-day responsibilities. It's really just that one specific situation at work.

Before this situation with your colleagues began two years ago, did you ever experience any period of time where you felt your thoughts were being broadcast to others, or felt like you were being controlled by an outside force?

No, I've never experienced anything like that. I've never felt like my thoughts were being broadcast or that I was being controlled by anything. It's just... normal thoughts. I've never had any issues like what you're describing, before this started or even now.

Have you experienced any significant periods of feeling unusually down, hopeless, or lacking in energy, or alternatively, periods where you felt unusually energetic, restless, or needing very little sleep?

No, I haven't really had anything like that. I mean, I get tired sometimes if I've been working late on a piece, but not... not unusually down or hopeless. And I definitely haven't had any times where I felt super energetic or like I didn't need to sleep. My mood and energy levels have been pretty normal, honestly. It's just the stress from what's happening with the ensemble that bothers me.
Have you ever used any substances, such as drugs or alcohol, that might have influenced your thoughts or experiences during these past two years?

No, I don't use any drugs. I mean, I might have a glass of wine with my wife at dinner sometimes, or a beer, but that's really it. I've never been into anything else. So I definitely haven't been taking or drinking anything that would... you know, mess with my head or make me imagine what's going on with them. I'm completely clear-headed.
When you are speaking with your colleagues or your wife, have they ever mentioned that they find it difficult to follow your train of thought or that your speech seems disorganized?

No, neither my wife nor my colleagues have ever said anything like that. I communicate pretty clearly. I mean, as a music director, I have to be very precise when I'm explaining things to the ensemble or going over a score. If I were disorganized or hard to follow, we wouldn't be able to rehearse properly at all. So, no, I haven't had any issues with my speech or my train of thought. Everyone understands me just fine.
Have you ever felt that there was something physically wrong with your body, such as a medical condition or an illness, that your doctors haven't been able to explain?

No, I haven't. Physically, I'm fine. I mean, I go for my regular checkups and nothing unusual has ever come up. I don't have any strange pains or illnesses, or anything like that. My body feels perfectly normal. It's really just the situation with the ensemble that's been the problem, not my health.
Have you ever sought out a therapist, counselor, or any other mental health professional regarding these specific concerns about your colleagues at any point during these past two years?

No, I haven't. I haven't seen a therapist or a counselor or anyone like that about this. I just... I haven't really felt the need to. I mean, it's a real situation happening at work, not something wrong with my mind. So, no, I haven't sought out any mental health professionals.
